links.outcome: Readability of LLM celiac disease patient education responses versus 6th-8th grade targets
links.effect: Gemini 2.0 median Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level 9.8 vs. 12.5 for both competitors (p < 0.001); all models exceeded recommended 6th-8th grade health literacy targets.
links.quote: However, all models exceeded recommended 6th-8th grade health literacy targets.

links.outcome: Misinformation presence in LLM responses to celiac disease patient questions
links.effect: Misinformation rates were 13.3% for Gemini 2.0, 23.3% for ChatGPT-4, and 24.2% for Claude 3.7; differences not significant (p = 0.778).
links.quote: While Gemini 2.0 showed numerically lower misinformation rates (13.3% vs. 23.3% for ChatGPT-4 and 24.2% for Claude 3.7), differences were not statistically significant (p = 0.778).

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates and compares the accuracy, readability, and misinformation rates of three LLMs (ChatGPT-4, Claude 3.7, Gemini 2.0) on patient education questions for celiac disease, evaluated by clinical experts.
